title: MCP Read-Only Hardening Implementation Spec v1 — Rig Relay
status: spec_draft — do not implement until reviewed

current_state_summary.real_dispatch: 10 of 16 tools return hardcoded stub data. Only 6 tools have any filesystem operation (_list_worktrees, _run_readonly_doctor, _summarize_dirty_state, _check_merge_friendly, _audit_dirty_state use subprocess; _build_context_packet, _create_consult_packet, _search_evidence, _read_receipt, etc. are stubs).
current_state_summary.descriptor_integrity: compute_tool_provenance_hash() exists but not called in dispatch path. Tool dispatch matches by bare string name with no hash verification.
current_state_summary.mutation_gate: Tier 4 check: any non-empty string passes. No cryptographic verification. No time-bound or scope-bound enforcement.
current_state_summary.auth: MCPPerUserAuthorization model exists but never instantiated. No actor_id, no user_id_hash, no scope enforcement, no expiry check.
current_state_summary.content_light: Server advertises content_light: True in initialize response. No actual scan performed on any tool output or resource response.
current_state_summary.common_envelope: 14 of 15 cross-surface envelope fields missing from all MCP responses. Only capability_id (tool name) and authority_tier present.
current_state_summary.roots: Tools use Path.cwd() directly. No workspace root boundary enforcement. No path traversal protection.
current_state_summary.transport: stdio (working). Streamable HTTP (deferred). Sync handler missing tools/call.

implementation_phases.description: Make every MCP tool dispatch verify the tool descriptor hash before execution. Without this, all other hardening is moot — a poisoned descriptor bypasses every gate.

steps.action: Add descriptor_hash field to MCPTool model
steps.detail: Generate provenance hash at model construction. Store as descriptor_hash: str on MCPTool.

steps.action: Build tool registry with hash index at server startup
steps.detail: Construct dict[descriptor_hash, MCPTool] alongside existing dict[name, MCPTool]. Verify no hash collisions.

steps.action: Verify descriptor hash BEFORE handler dispatch in call_tool()
steps.detail: Before _dispatch(), compute current hash of the resolved tool descriptor. If mismatch with registered hash, refuse with refusal envelope (refusal_code: 'descriptor_integrity_failure').

steps.action: Re-run compute_tool_provenance_hash on every tools/list response
steps.detail: On tools/list, re-compute provenance hashes for all tools. Any hash mismatch → log warning + exclude tool from response. Track drift count as telemetry event.

steps.action: Run classify_tool_descriptor_suspicious on every tools/list response
steps.detail: For every tool in tools/list, run the suspicious classifier. Flagged tools → log warning + emit governance telemetry event (severity: warning). Do not serve flagged descriptors to clients.

implementation_phases.description: Enforce workspace root boundaries on all tools that access the filesystem. Reject path traversal with refusal envelope.

steps.action: Accept workspace_root parameter in RigMCPServer constructor
steps.detail: Default to Path.cwd().resolve(). Store as self._workspace_root.

steps.action: Add resolve_safe_path() call before any Path.cwd() usage
steps.detail: Wrap all filesystem tool handlers (_list_worktrees, _run_readonly_doctor, _summarize_dirty_state, _check_merge_friendly, _audit_dirty_state) with workspace root validation. Reject any request targeting paths outside workspace_root.

steps.action: Add allowed_roots validation for resources
steps.detail: Validate that resource URIs (rig://*) resolve to safe paths within workspace_root before serving content. Reject with refusal envelope if out-of-bounds.

steps.action: Emit refusal envelope on boundary violation
steps.detail: Schema: rig.relay.mcp.refusal.v1. refusal_code: 'workspace_boundary_violation'.

implementation_phases.description: Scan every MCP tool output and resource response for sensitive content before returning to client. Apply content classification.

steps.action: Integrate redaction.py content-light scanner into MCP response path
steps.detail: After _dispatch() returns a result dict, pass it through content-light scanner. Classify as: public_safe, private_local, sensitive_metadata, secret_bearing, forbidden_raw.

steps.action: Refuse responses containing secret-bearing or forbidden-raw content
steps.detail: If scan detects tokens (sk-*, Bearer *, etc.), absolute home paths, or raw file content, refuse the response with refusal envelope. refusal_code: 'content_light_violation'.

steps.action: Add content_light_classification to every response
steps.detail: Every successful response includes content_light_classification field with one of the 5 values above. List methods (tools/list, resources/list, prompts/list) include top-level content_light: true.

steps.action: Add SHA256 hashing for any file-content-adjacent data
steps.detail: Replace any file content references (e.g. _run_readonly_doctor output, _summarize_dirty_state output) with SHA256 hashes only. No raw file paths beyond workspace-relative.

implementation_phases.description: Wrap every MCP tool call result in a common evidence envelope with all 15 cross-surface fields. Emit rig.relay.tool.* telemetry events.

steps.action: Define MCP evidence envelope model
steps.detail: Add MCPEvidenceEnvelope to models.py with: request_id, session_id, actor_id, surface='mcp', authority_tier, capability_id, input_hash, output_hash, payload_schema, policy_decision_id, approval_receipt_id (if applicable), trace_id, artifact_refs, content_light_classification, redaction_scan_id, source_of_truth_refs, timestamp, producer.

steps.action: Wrap every call_tool response in evidence envelope
steps.detail: Before returning result, build envelope with computed hashes and metadata. Result dict becomes envelope.payload. Envelope is the JSON-RPC result, not the raw tool output.

steps.action: Emit rig.relay.tool.called telemetry event per invocation
steps.detail: On every successful (non-refused) tool call, emit structured telemetry event with all envelope fields. Content-light only — no raw output in telemetry.

steps.action: Add policy_decision_id generation
steps.detail: For tier 0-2 tools: policy_decision_id = hash(descriptor_hash + 'allowed_read_only'). For tier 3: policy_decision_id = hash(descriptor_hash + 'blocked_pending_approval'). Document the decision.

implementation_phases.description: Implement local-first MCP auth for read-only surface. Stdio-bound trust model with per-session token and scoped authorization.

steps.action: Generate session token at server startup
steps.detail: On server.serve_stdio(), generate a local session token (SHA256 of PID + timestamp). Store as self._session_token. Emit token to stdout as first JSON-RPC notification.

steps.action: Require session_token in every tools/call request params
steps.detail: Every tools/call request must include session_token matching the server-generated token. Mismatch → refusal envelope (refusal_code: 'unauthorized').

steps.action: Instantiate MCPPerUserAuthorization per request
steps.detail: On each tools/call, build MCPPerUserAuthorization with user_id_hash (derived from session_token), scopes_granted (from tier), authorization_status, and expiry.

steps.action: Enforce tier-specific scope requirements
steps.detail: Tier 0: rig:read. Tier 1: rig:read + rig:analyze. Tier 2: rig:read + rig:validate. Tier 3+: blocked (rig:propose, rig:mutate, rig:release not granted). Check scopes_granted against required scopes. Mismatch → refusal.

steps.action: Add future hosted extension point
steps.detail: Document where bearer/OAuth token validation hooks would be inserted. Add MCPToolAuthMetadata.bearer_supported / oauth_supported fields as future flags. Do not implement hosted auth in this phase.

can_parallelize: Phase 2 (roots) can run alongside Phase 3 (content-light) after Phase 1 completes
gating_phases: Phase 1 blocks all subsequent phases — no hardening without descriptor integrity
Phases 2-4 must complete before Phase 5 (auth) can be meaningful
hardening_sequencing.estimated_effort: Phase 1: small. Phase 2: small. Phase 3: medium. Phase 4: medium. Phase 5: small. Total: ~1-2 weeks for full P0 + P1 surface.

what_must_not_be_done: Do not expose tier 4-5 tools in read-only surface — hard-block at call_tool() dispatch
Do not implement bearer/OAuth auth — local session token only for P0/P1
Do not surface mutation tools until cryptographic approval receipts exist
Do not serve raw file content in any MCP response
Do not allow tools/call without descriptor hash verification
Do not skip content-light scan on any response path
Do not implement streamable HTTP until stdio path is fully hardened
Do not add new MCP tools without adding them to the descriptor integrity registry
